newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RESEARCH ALERT-Oil Search rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Oil Search rated a buy.

text.p: Brokerage house Wilson HTM Ltd said it was recommending Oil Search Ltd as a buy investment, reflecting the oil and gas explorer's significant stake in the Moran field in Papua New Guinea (PNG).

"We have upgraded our reserve estimate for Moran to 500 million barrels plus. This is the biggest oil field discovered to date in PNG," Wilson's resources research director, Phil Hutchings said in a report.
Hutchings said Oil Search was calculated to have average equity of around 17 percent in the greater Moran structure.

In addition to the upside from Moran, there was further exploration potential in Oil Search's fold belt permits plus the potential for commercialising large gas reserves, he said. He said Wilson had modelled a 350 million barrel reserve scenario.
"Our development assumptions include capital expenditure of US$800 million with production starting in 1999," he said.

The combination of the Moran, Kutubu and Gobe fields production generated earnings of more than 30 cents a share after the year 2000 and cash flow of A$100 million annually, putting Oil Search on a price-earnings of 12 times, he said.
"Importantly the cash flow from Gobe can be used to largely finance Moran development, leaving Oil Search with little debt," the report said.
Oil Search shares closed at A$4.19 on Tuesday, up two cents.
At the time of the writing of the report on July 25, Oil Search shares were at A$3.74.
The stock has traded between A$2.37 and A$4.18 this year.
Oil Search reported a net profit of A$24.05 million in the 1996 calendar year, up from A$22.84 million a year earlier.
